purpose: Targeted pollution<->waste test error audit of 12 protected benchmark candidates
taxonomy_authority: Exp04 audit definitions + Exp05 KEEP precedent + metadata CSV subcategories

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Sandy beach shore heavily littered with plastic bottles, packaging, and debris; visually indistinguishable from waste-class litter_accumulation / waterway_waste precedent
candidates.independent_reasoning: Solid litter (bottles, bags, branded containers) scattered on beach shore = classic waste class. No chemical/toxic contamination visible. Matches waste subcategory litter_accumulation / waterway_waste precedent in metadata CSV.
candidates.scene_description: Sandy beach shore with scattered plastic bottles, bags, debris, IPA Andina branded blue plastic container, bamboo sticks

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Roadside illegal dumping of furniture scrap, concrete rings, household junk in forested rural context; fits waste subcategory roadside_dumping
candidates.independent_reasoning: Roadside discarded concrete culvert rings + household junk/appliance scrap = solid waste dumping. Fits roadside_dumping waste subcategory exactly. No chemical or industrial pollution visible. Exp05 flooding prediction is an Exp05-only model failure (confuses wet dirt road for flooding), but subject itself = waste.
candidates.scene_description: Forested dirt road with 4 large concrete ring culverts on left, household junk/appliance scrap dumping on right, NO ENTRY sign on barrier
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Roadside dumping of solid construction + household waste

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Ravine slope discarded plastic sacks, packaging, bottles, shoes = dense residential garbage dump; matches garbage_accumulation waste subcategory
candidates.independent_reasoning: Closest-cropped dense garbage dump image in set: Pepsi bottles, plastic sacks, shoes, barrels on ravine slope. Classic garbage_accumulation. All 4 experiments predict waste >99%. STRONGEST label-noise signal of all 12.
candidates.scene_description: Close-up of dense garbage dump on rocky/mossy ravine slope: plastic Pepsi bottles, plastic bags, shoes, barrels
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Dense solid garbage accumulation in ravine

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Hillside slope dumped computer monitors and e-waste classified by Exp04 as solid waste dumping
candidates.independent_reasoning: ELECTRONIC WASTE = hazardous-toxic contamination class. CRT monitors, keyboards, circuits contain lead, mercury, cadmium, heavy metals, brominated flame retardants — not merely inert solid waste. Pollution KEEP criteria include chemical/toxic contamination. This is the ONLY protected candidate for which pollution label is taxonomically defensible under project rules. All 4 experiments correctly predict pollution, consistent with model learning the e-waste = pollution signal.
candidates.scene_description: Dry grassy hillside, jumbled pile of computer monitors, keyboards, yellow plastic crates, hoses, tires, household junk (e-waste dump)
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Electronic waste (CRT monitors + electronics) dumping with toxic contamination aspect

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Alleyway ditch littered with food wrappers, plastic bags, packaging, metal containers near stone wall drain
candidates.independent_reasoning: Dense alleyway domestic trash: food packaging, bottles, metal containers, black bags near drain. Matches litter_accumulation / garbage_accumulation waste subcategory exactly. No chemical or industrial contamination.
candidates.scene_description: Alleyway rocky/dirt ditch, dense mixed domestic trash food packaging, plastic bottles, metal containers, wooden planks, black bags near stone wall with drain
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Domestic litter accumulation in alleyway ditch

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Woods hillside illegal dumping discarded vehicle tires among trees/ivy
candidates.independent_reasoning: Illegal tire dump in wooded hillside. Tires = solid waste; also environmental hazard but under project taxonomy, dumped tires fit roadside_dumping / garbage_accumulation (as inert solid mass). While tires leach chemicals long-term, the project precedent (Exp04 reasoning for other tire scenes) classifies illegal tire dumps as waste. Label noise.
candidates.scene_description: Wooded hillside, numerous discarded black rubber tires scattered among trees/ivy (illegal tire dump)
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Illegal tire dumping in wooded area

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Dumped pile of weathered concrete blocks and bricks on open dirt lot in park-like setting = fly-tipped construction scrap
candidates.independent_reasoning: Abandoned weathered concrete slab pile with embedded red bricks on open field — no active construction, no workers, no machinery, no buildings under construction. Project taxonomy KEEP-as-pollution rule for construction = ACTIVE construction with machinery/workers (POL_215/224/225/238/242/247/249 precedent). Inert fly-tipped construction rubble = waste (matches WST_001 construction_scrap precedent).
candidates.scene_description: Large weathered mossy concrete slab pile with embedded broken red bricks, dry leafless brush, distant park-like field with trees/bare winter branches
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Fly-tipped concrete/brick rubble in open field

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Commercial building boards, plastic tarps, metal poles dumped behind building on gravel; no active construction
candidates.independent_reasoning: Dumped construction scrap (panels, tarps, pipes, ladder wood) behind commercial fence — no workers, no machinery, no active building work. Matches Exp04 fly-tipped construction_scrap waste precedent WST_001. Inert material improperly discarded = waste.
candidates.scene_description: Fenced commercial/industrial yard (metal fence, building with dark roof, white van behind fence), dumped on gravel: large white panels/boards, black tarp, rusted pipes, wooden ladder pieces
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Fly-tipped commercial construction scrap in industrial yard

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Illegal roadside dumping of black garbage bags, furniture, drywall, boards with cleanup crew and pickup truck present
candidates.independent_reasoning: Massive roadside overflowing dump pile — drywall, furniture, garbage bags, cabinet drawers. Workers present are CLEANUP CREW (safety gear + truck hauling bags away), not active construction crew. Scene context: this is a roadside_dumping being remediated. Matches roadside_dumping waste subcategory exactly. All 4 experiments predict waste.
candidates.scene_description: Unpaved rural road, massive overflowing roadside dump pile: drywall sheets, insulation, wooden boards, furniture, black garbage bags, cabinet drawers + 3 cleanup workers in safety gear + white pickup truck
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Massive roadside illegal dumping with cleanup crew in progress

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Pile of dumped broken terracotta roof tiles and concrete slabs with mortar
candidates.independent_reasoning: Extreme close-up of dumped broken roof tiles + concrete chunks + brick. No active construction context. Dumped/discarded construction rubble from prior demolition. Exp01-03 all predicted pollution strongly (~97%) but Exp05 after sanitized training now correctly predicts waste (51.85% borderline). This is a training-distribution effect: Exp05 saw similar roof tiles classified as waste in train/val and learned the pattern. Classification: fly-tipped construction waste = waste.
candidates.scene_description: EXTREME CLOSE-UP of jumbled broken terracotta roof tiles + concrete chunks with mortar + red brick pieces

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Roadside pile of plastic sacks containing rubble and construction scrap near urban construction site with blue tarps
candidates.independent_reasoning: Urban scene with blue tarps at ACTIVE construction site, but the specific subject being classified is a PILE OF PLASTIC SACKS filled with rubble/earth + discarded tricycle on top. These are waste sacks placed OUTSIDE the site's boundary (muddy puddles, curbside position) = improper disposal. Exp02/03/05 all predict waste strongly; active-construction elements are background context, not the dominant phenomenon. Dominant = fly-tipped construction waste bags = waste.
candidates.scene_description: Urban construction site with blue tarps/temporary fencing + multi-story buildings, pile of dirty plastic sacks (yellow, green, white, blue) filled with rubble/earth, broken tricycle rickshaw on top of sacks, muddy puddles
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Fly-tipped rubble-filled plastic sacks curbside near active construction

candidates.exp04_reasoning: Curbside street pile of cardboard, white sacks, plaster rubble near multi-story building with fish murals
candidates.independent_reasoning: BORDERLINE between (a) construction dust/pollution from active street renovation and (b) curbside fly-tipped waste. Plaster rubble + concrete tile fragments + dirt = could be from active construction near curbside (pollution KEEP). But also cardboard boxes + white sacks + garbage bags + orange food trash on ground = clearly mixed with municipal waste. Exp03 correctly predicted pollution (56.31% vs 38.05% waste); Exp05 now predicts waste (64.47%). The visual mix of both signals = genuinely ambiguous. Both interpretations are defensible; insufficient evidence for a forced call.
candidates.scene_description: Urban street in front of multi-story building with fish murals, large rubble pile (concrete, tile fragments, dirt) + stacked brown paper/cardboard bags + torn white plastic bags + black garbage bags, orange on ground (likely food trash)
candidates.dominant_phenomenon: Mixed construction dust/plaster rubble + curbside garbage bags (mixed signals)
